reviews.author: Thomas Zimmermann
reviews.summary: Reviewer Thomas Zimmermann noted that the patch does not include the necessary header file inclusion for __nonnull_args() in drm_gem.h, and suggested including <linux/compiler_attributes.h> to fix this.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi

Am 28.10.26 um 09:19 schrieb Dmitry Ilvokhin:
> Commit 22302af28d3f ("cleanup: Annotate guard constructors with
> nonnull") added the macro __nonnull_args() to wrap raw compiler
> attribute.
>
> Replace __attribute__((nonnull)) with __nonnull_args() to standardize
> nonnull attribute usage across the tree and keep the attribute's quirks
> in one place rather than open-coded at every call site.
>
> Suggested-by: Miguel Ojeda <miguel.ojeda.sandonis@gmail.com>
> Signed-off-by: Dmitry Ilvokhin <d@ilvokhin.com>

Reviewed-by: Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de>

Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?

Best regards
Thomas

> ---
>   include/drm/drm_gem.h | 2 +-
>   1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)
>
> diff --git a/include/drm/drm_gem.h b/include/drm/drm_gem.h
> index ed329408acbe..56dd15921c7a 100644
> --- a/include/drm/drm_gem.h
> +++ b/include/drm/drm_gem.h
> @@ -566,7 +566,7 @@ static inline void drm_gem_object_get(struct drm_gem_object *obj)
>   	kref_get(&obj->refcount);
>   }
>   
> -__attribute__((nonnull))
> +__nonnull_args()
>   static inline void
>   __drm_gem_object_put(struct drm_gem_object *obj)
>   {

--

reviews.author: Miguel Ojeda
reviews.summary: Reviewer Miguel Ojeda pointed out that the patch does not handle the inclusion of <linux/compiler_attributes.h> correctly, specifically in the file drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_ttm.c, and suggested that it should be included only if custom compiler flags are being used.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32 AM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
>
> Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?

No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
custom with the compiler flags etc.).

I hope that helps!

Cheers,
Miguel

reviews.author: Andy Shevchenko
reviews.summary: Reviewer Andy Shevchenko pointed out that the inclusion of <linux/compiler_attributes.h> should be handled by the build machinery, and suggested cleaning up headers that directly pull in compiler_types/compile_attributes or kconfig.h.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> >
> > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> 
> No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> custom with the compiler flags etc.).

Usually it comes to the mere drivers via types.h, in rare cases (usually some
more generic library headers, we do better granularity as it affects the almost
entire kernel. Just double check that types.h is explicitly included.

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko

---

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 01:12:06PM +0000, Dmitry Ilvokhin wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> > On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> > >
> > > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> > 
> > No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> > custom with the compiler flags etc.).
> 
> Just to add a bit more colour to Miguel's reply.
> 
> I believe idea behind include/linux/compiler_attributes.h is to make
> attribute wrappers as simple and transparent to use as native compiler
> attributes. In particular, this means they should be available in every
> kernel compilation unit without any additional effort.
> 
> For this reason, all the nessesary plumbing is handled at the build
> machinery level (see scripts/Makefile.lib:171), where '-include'
> compiler flag is used to pull in include/linux/compiler_types.h, which
> in turn pulls include/linux/compiler_attributes.h.

Ah, TIL! Please, discard my comment then. Perhaps we need to clean up all
headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly (the same way
we do for kconfig.h).

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko

2026-10-29.patch_summary: This patch series replaces open-coded uses of the __attribute__((nonnull)) macro with the __nonnull_args() macro, which is a wrapper that keeps the quirks of the attribute in one place. The goal is to standardize nonnull attribute usage across the Linux kernel tree. The patches can be applied separately and are build-tested on various configurations. Some instances of __attribute__((nonnull)) remain in the tools subdirectory and should be updated separately after this patchset lands.
